title: How the day ended
text: Stocks jumped today. The S&P 500 fund SPY rose 2.4% to $752.64, and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ rose 3.5% to $679.35. Almost every company on our list went up. The big exception was NVIDIA, which fell 4.3%. Reports said lower oil prices helped the mood. Tomorrow, watch whether the chip makers keep their gains. One strong day after a hard drop does not tell us what comes next.

title: Nearly everything rose, but NVIDIA fell
text: NVIDIA dropped 4.3% to $178.67 while the other four AI supplier companies rose. AMD gained 13.3%, Vertiv 10.8%, Broadcom 8.8% and TSMC 3.5%. On average the five AI suppliers rose 6.4%. The four big AI companies (Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta) rose 3.0% on average, and Meta led them with 5.1%. News reports linked NVIDIA's drop to stories about its CEO. NVIDIA is still about 27% below its 52 week high.

title: The wildest movers of the day
text: Rocket Lab rose 10.9% and Vertiv rose 10.8%. AMD's 13.3% jump was the biggest on the list. These companies have high betas (2.1 to 2.6), so they move much more than the market, up or down. Their risk scores are 7.8 to 10 out of 10. AMD also has a P/E of about 109, which means investors pay $109 for each $1 of yearly profit. That price already expects a lot of growth.

title: Rates are still the quiet worry
text: Today felt calm, but the 10 year Treasury yield averaged 5.13% in October, the highest in the last 12 months. High rates make safe bonds more attractive and can pull money away from stocks, especially fast growing tech. Utilities (up 3.6%) and industrial companies (up 3.2%) led the sectors today, while financial companies were flat.

title: Lesson 43: What is correlation?
text: Correlation means how much two things move together. Today is a good example. Almost every stock on our list went up at the same time, because the whole market felt better. When stocks move together, we say they are highly correlated. This matters for safety. If you own five stocks that all rise and fall together, you are not really spread out. Owning different kinds of things, like a dividend fund, a health company and a tech company, can help because they do not always move the same way. Notice that NVIDIA fell today while its rivals rose. Stocks can also go their own way when there is news about one company.
